argument_markdown:
Source-backed input: RED-0001 consists of the pairs (3,12), (5,8), (6,6), (7,4), (8,0), (8,1), and (8,2).

Proved counterexample: take the one-edge separating dual graph with vertices v_5 and v_0 of genera 5 and 0. Put markings 1 through 6 on v_5 and markings 7 and 8 on v_0. Including the half-edge of the node, the corresponding factor pairs are (5,7) and (0,3). The graph has total genus 5 and eight legs. Both vertices are stable because 2·5−2+7=15>0 and 2·0−2+3=1>0.

The associated clutching morphism is Mbar_{5,7} × Mbar_{0,3} → Mbar_{5,8}. Its image is the irreducible separating boundary divisor whose rational component carries markings 7 and 8. One factor therefore has genus 5. This directly contradicts the clause in the exact theorem that every separating product has factors of genus at most 4; the additional genus-3 clause does not include this factor.

The counterexample does not put a RED-0001 pair on the boundary: (5,7) and (0,3) are both outside the displayed residual list. Thus it refutes precisely the asserted exhaustive genus description after the colon, not the narrower outside-RED-0001 conclusion that could be repaired by adding the genus-5 case n≤7. No Tate assertion, compact-cohomology conclusion, boundary-image conclusion, or claim about H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8};Q) is made. No computation or unproved hypothesis is used, and there is no remaining gap.

claims.statement: The one-edge graph with genus-5 and genus-0 vertices, six legs on the former and two legs on the latter, is a stable dual graph of type (5,8).
Its clutching stratum is the irreducible separating boundary divisor represented by Mbar_{5,7} × Mbar_{0,3}.
The genus-5 factor Mbar_{5,7} contradicts the exact theorem's assertion that every separating product has factors of genus at most 4.
The pairs (5,7) and (0,3) are outside RED-0001, so the counterexample makes no claim that a RED-0001 pair occurs on this boundary.

summary: The theorem as written is false because the stable rational-tail boundary divisor Mbar_{5,7} × Mbar_{0,3} has a genus-5 factor, contradicting the asserted genus-at-most-4 description, although neither factor belongs to RED-0001.
theorem_statement: Every irreducible boundary stratum of Mbar_{5,8} is a pair (g,n) outside the RED-0001 residual list: the non-separating divisor has normalization Mbar_{4,10}, and every separating product has factors of genus at most 4, or of genus 3 with at most 9 markings. This theorem makes no Tate assertion and does not conclude H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8};Q).
